I added `TaskStore.rename_many(updates)` in `src/tasklib/store.py`, and the visible tests pass (127 passed). I didn't add tests for the new method, so its own behavior is only covered by my reading of the spec.

- **Validation:** it first checks every entry. Each must be a dict with exactly `id` and `title`, the ID must be valid, the title must be valid (it's trimmed), and IDs can't repeat. Any of these failing raises `ValueError`.
- **Missing IDs:** after that it looks up all the IDs, and a valid ID that isn't in the store raises `KeyError`.
- **Applying changes:** titles are only changed once every check has passed, so a bad batch leaves all tasks unchanged. Order, priorities, completion flags and the next-ID counter are never touched.
- **Return value:** it returns the stored `Task` objects in request order. An empty list returns `[]`.
